parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation and no documented visitor entry friction; gender-reassignment discrimination protection survives the April 2025 biological-sex ruling, and courts function. But the combined regime imposes documented universal exposures: strip-search and custody searching by birth sex, birth-sex prison placement, a statutory single-sex-spaces code (in force Aug 2026) covering hostels, changing rooms and medical services, announced ward exclusion for trans patients, and a documented death following ward removal. Regional hate-crime coverage is partial; minors' gender care is effectively closed. Media and official framing is hostile. Worst feature is tier-1 state-imposed facility exclusion without a working remedy yet, holding it to Elevated Risk despite functioning rule of law and retained anti-discrimination protection.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry or document rules for visitors are established by the dossier; GRCs' 'for all purposes' effect was narrowed by the 2025 ruling for equality-act purposes, and foreign GRCs from 50 jurisdictions are no longer accepted (mainly an applicant-facing rule).
entry_documents.protection: No documented border refusal, secondary screening or marker scrutiny of transgender visitors; discrimination on gender reassignment remains protected.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could still interact with single-sex-space and custody rules if it prompts scrutiny.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Transport police (post-April 2025) strip-search trans women by officers of their sex at birth; a region's June 2025 interim guidance conducts custody and stop-and-search above jacket level on biological sex; a region's guidance allowing birth-sex prison placement was struck down June 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Regional guidance offers an officer of lived gender on request; government defends individual risk assessments; courts review custody practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document or presentation dispute can escalate into detention, where birth-sex searching and placement then apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Statutory single-sex-spaces code in force 5 Aug 2026 (hostels, changing rooms, medical services, communal accommodation) interpreted on biological sex; UN experts warn it institutionalises discrimination; trans-patient ward ban announced as policy plan.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Gender-reassignment discrimination protection retained; one region on different equality legislation still assessing; legal challenge at pre-action stage; large LGBT communities in cities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using ordinary accommodation, swimming, or a hospital can meet the code simultaneously with the 2025 ruling's biological reading.

care_services.exposure: A trans woman removed from an available cancer ward bed to a side room, delayed 16 days from pain management, died unsurvivably; ward-ban plans announced. For minors: puberty blockers stopped (2024, indefinite), no new hormones to minors, national youth service closed, only 2 of 8 regional centres open.
care_services.protection: Adult gender-affirming care formally available via NHS or privately; 2002 policy states transsexualism is not mental illness; discrimination protection covers care access.
care_services.interaction: A visitor's injury or illness can trigger discovery and ward placement decisions by biological sex.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Media anti-trans rhetoric described as vitriolic since 2016-2018; ministerial rhetoric reversing diversity measures and pronoun guidance; rainbow-index rank fell from 1st (86%, 2015) to 22nd (45%, 2025); UN warning the code risks institutionalised discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Equality-act protection on gender reassignment retained for visitors; 86% poll acceptance of homosexuality (no trans-specific poll); functioning independent courts.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile official framing raises the chance that routine facility or service encounters are resolved against the visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Youth gender care effectively closed (no blockers, no new hormones, service closed, 2 of 8 centres); trans girls barred from a trust's schools without GRC (2022) and from girls' rugby teams under-12s (2022); single-sex space code affects a child's school, changing and ward settings.
minors_guardians.protection: Transgender youth covered by the national equality act; parents can seek judicial review (2021 appeal restored under-16 consent route, though service now closed).
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's minor can be excluded from facilities or care while the parent faces the same single-sex-space rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2025 survey of trans/intersex/gender-nonconforming respondents corroborates fear of harassment in public gendered spaces; gender-identity hate-crime and hate-speech protection exists only in some regions; no documented pattern of violence against visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime protection in some regions; retained equality protection; no documented state tolerance of violence; no trans-specific killing pattern in dossier.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Partial regional coverage means recourse after an assault depends on which nation the visitor is in.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Code's practical application unresolved; legal challenge only at pre-action stage; one region's impact assessment ongoing; one police searching policy unretrievable (403); inquest and negligence claim unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts demonstrably act (striking down prison guidance, hearing challenges); equality claims available; international scrutiny from UN experts; advocacy and legal-clinic infrastructure present.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate but post-date or trail the hostile practices, so exposure persists while litigation runs.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Vesskar, this dossier shows routine exposure at clinics, transport-security and single-sex facilities with documented detention-adjacent humiliation (birth-sex searches) and denial of care, plus slow, narrow remedies. It rates somewhat higher because no entry friction, no trans-specific criminal statute or prosecutions are documented, and anti-discrimination protection survives; lower than Vesskar nowhere material.

Marisol Union's ward placement by document sex with delayed treatment and functioning but slow advocates closely parallels the ward and facility exposure here. This dossier is worse on severity (a documented death from ward removal, an official ward-ban plan, closed youth care) and better on entry; net similar, so comparable rating.

Meridia combines trained border staff, brief detention with written reasons, counsel access and compensation. This jurisdiction lacks those documented visitor-facing assurances, has actively narrowed trans protections since 2023-2026, and imposes birth-sex searching and facility exclusion; it must rate materially below this anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces no criminalisation, no documented border obstacle and working courts, with gender-reassignment discrimination protection surviving the 2025 ruling. The combined regime nonetheless operates biological-sex rules at the points a visitor actually meets the state and institutions: custody and strip searching by birth sex, birth-sex prison placement, a statutory single-sex-spaces code covering accommodation, changing and medical spaces, announced ward exclusion, and a documented fatal care delay after ward removal. Regional variation (hate-crime coverage, one region still assessing) adds unpredictability. Youth care is effectively closed for a visiting minor. Hostile official and media framing raises discovery friction, while litigation and UN warnings show recourse exists but does not yet reverse the exposure — placing this at mid Elevated Risk.
